name: MiniMax
note: Quota only. MiniMax reports one window per model in a list rather than a keyed object, so the window key is the model name. This descriptor is the international region; the China region ships as `minimax-cn`, reading its own key file rather than this one's variable, so a user with MINIMAX_API_KEY set gets no second gauge against a region their key is not for. That replaces an instruction to override `quota.endpoint` by hand, which asked a user to edit JSON for something a differently-named key file now does. Model names come back verbatim, so badges/labels are declared for the models MiniMax ships today; an unlisted model still charts, abbreviated from its name. The key is read from MINIMAX_API_KEY when Antarium was started from a shell, and from ~/.antarium/keys/minimax otherwise — an app launched from Finder inherits the launchd session environment rather than a shell's, so the file is the route that always works. The endpoint is published nowhere; checked 2026-09-22, platform.minimax.io/docs/token-plan says only that the quota "is shown as a usage bar in the console". The fixture is the whole of the check. `current_interval_usage_count` is read as what REMAINS, not what was spent, which is the opposite of what the name says and was got wrong here until 2026-09-24. The endpoint is `coding_plan/remains` and the list is `model_remains`; three independent readings agree — ClaudeBar's probe records a dashboard cross-check (a console showing 3% used against usage_count 1459 of 1500), an openclaw issue reports the same inversion, and a third tool derives used = total - remaining from it. Read as consumption the bar was inverted in the direction that matters: it stayed green while the quota ran out. Probed 2026-09-27 with an invalid token: this endpoint answers HTTP 200 with {"base_resp":{"status_code":1004,"status_msg":"cookie is missing, log in again"}}, so UsageHTTP's 401 handling never fires. needsAuthWhen matches status_code 1004 specifically — the code whose own message says to log in again — rather than any non-zero code, since the other 1xxx codes mean other things.

compatibility.note: Mapping is fixture-verified against the published response shape; the numbers themselves are unconfirmed against a live plan.
